ref: Tests of similarity of triangles SolvedEx.1
stem: In \(\triangle XYZ\), \(\angle Y = 100^\circ\), \(\angle Z = 30^\circ\), In \(\triangle LMN\), \(\angle M = 100^\circ\), \(\angle N = 30^\circ\), Are \(\triangle XYZ\) and \(\triangle LMN\) similar? If yes, by which test?
solution:
In \(\triangle XYZ\) and \(\triangle LMN\),

\(\angle Y = 100^\circ\), \(\angle M = 100^\circ\), \(\therefore \angle Y \cong \angle M\)

\(\angle Z = 30^\circ\), \(\angle N = 30^\circ\), \(\therefore \angle Z \cong \angle N\)

\(\therefore \triangle XYZ \sim \triangle LMN\) ..... by AA test.

ref: Tests of similarity of triangles SolvedEx.2
stem:
Are two triangles in figure 1.51 similar, according to the information given? If yes, by which test?

(Fig. 1.51 prints PM = 6 and MN = 10 in \(\triangle PMN\), UV = 3 and VW = 5 in \(\triangle UVW\), and marks \(\angle M \cong \angle V\).)
solution:
In \(\triangle PMN\) and \(\triangle UVW\)

\(\frac{PM}{UV} = \frac{6}{3} = \frac{2}{1}\), \(\frac{MN}{VW} = \frac{10}{5} = \frac{2}{1}\)

\(\therefore \frac{PM}{UV} = \frac{MN}{VW}\)

and \(\angle M \cong \angle V\) ......... Given

\(\triangle PMN \sim \triangle UVW\) ......... SAS test of similarity
note: Fig. 1.51 prints PM = 6, MN = 10 in \(\triangle PMN\) and UV = 3, VW = 5 in \(\triangle UVW\), with \(\angle M\) and \(\angle V\) marked congruent.

ref: Tests of similarity of triangles SolvedEx.3
stem:
Can we say that the two triangles in figure 1.52 similar, according to information given? If yes, by which test?

(Fig. 1.52 prints XY = 14 and YZ = 20 in \(\triangle XYZ\), MN = 21 and NP = 30 in \(\triangle MNP\), and marks \(\angle Z \cong \angle P\).)
solution:
\(\triangle XYZ\) and \(\triangle MNP\),

\(\frac{XY}{MN} = \frac{14}{21} = \frac{2}{3}\),

\(\frac{YZ}{NP} = \frac{20}{30} = \frac{2}{3}\)

It is given that \(\angle Z \cong \angle P\).

But \(\angle Z\) and \(\angle P\) are not included angles by sides which are in proportion.

\(\therefore \triangle XYZ\) and \(\triangle MNP\) can not be said to be similar.
note: Fig. 1.52 prints XY = 14, YZ = 20 in \(\triangle XYZ\) and MN = 21, NP = 30 in \(\triangle MNP\), with \(\angle Z\) and \(\angle P\) marked congruent.

ref: Tests of similarity of triangles SolvedEx.4
stem: In the adjoining figure 1.53 BP \(\perp\) AC, CQ \(\perp\) AB, A \(-\) P \(-\) C, A \(-\) Q \(-\) B, then prove that \(\triangle APB\) and \(\triangle AQC\) are similar.
solution:
In \(\triangle APB\) and \(\triangle AQC\)

\(\angle APB = 90^\circ\) .......... (I)

\(\angle AQC = 90^\circ\) .......... (II)

\(\therefore \angle APB \cong \angle AQC\) .... from (I) and (II)

\(\angle PAB \cong \angle QAC\) .... (common angle)

\(\therefore \triangle APB \sim \triangle AQC\) ..... AA test
note: The book prints this solution with three blanks (the two right-angle measures and the reason for \(\angle PAB \cong \angle QAC\)); they are filled in here so the stored solution is a complete worked answer.

ref: Tests of similarity of triangles SolvedEx.5
stem: Diagonals of a quadrilateral ABCD intersect in point Q. If 2QA = QC, 2QB = QD, then prove that DC = 2AB.
solution:
Given : 2QA = QC, 2QB = QD

To prove : CD = 2AB

Proof : 2QA = QC \(\therefore \frac{QA}{QC} = \frac{1}{2}\) .......... (I)

2QB = QD \(\therefore \frac{QB}{QD} = \frac{1}{2}\) .......... (II)

\(\therefore \frac{QA}{QC} = \frac{QB}{QD}\) .......... from (I) and (II)

In \(\triangle AQB\) and \(\triangle CQD\),

\(\frac{QA}{QC} = \frac{QB}{QD}\) .......... proved

\(\angle AQB \cong \angle DQC\) .......... opposite angles

\(\therefore \triangle AQB \sim \triangle CQD\) .......... (SAS test of similarity)

\(\therefore \frac{AQ}{CQ} = \frac{QB}{QD} = \frac{AB}{CD}\) .......... corresponding sides are proportional

But \(\frac{AQ}{CQ} = \frac{1}{2}\) \(\therefore \frac{AB}{CD} = \frac{1}{2}\)

\(\therefore 2AB = CD\)
